purpose: Prevent agent overclaiming while preserving clear structural reporting, model-relative facts, simulation outcomes, and real-world comparisons.

core_rule.statement: No unrestricted ontological, physical, mathematical, or universal truth claims may be made from framework structure, metaphor, simulation, analogy, or internal consistency alone.
core_rule.allowed_output_mode: Report what was observed, defined, simulated, compared, or structurally mapped, with explicit scope.

must_use: This does not establish external physical truth...
The comparison is analogical, not an identity claim...
must_not_use_unqualified: is the actual mechanism of nature

allowed.C0_definition: Internal definition, terminology, or notation only.
allowed.C1_model_relative: Statement valid only inside the declared framework or formal scaffold.
allowed.C2_simulation_observed: Outcome observed within a declared simulation/config/seed regime.
allowed.C3_structural_comparison: Comparison to external theory/data as resemblance, analogy, or contrast only.
allowed.C4_supported_internal: Internally supported by multiple governed mechanisms, tests, and falsification attempts.
allowed.C5_external_claim: Requires external peer review, independent reproduction, and domain evidence; blocked by default.

claim_classes.external_claim_policy: C5 claims are prohibited unless explicitly authorized and evidence-certified.

non_occlusion_requirements: Do not hide uncertainty behind vague humility language.
Do not soften claims so much that mechanisms become unclear.
Always expose scope, evidence type, and failure conditions.
Always preserve negative results, null results, NaN results, failed tests, and boundary cases.
required_output_structure_for_reports: What was directly defined or observed
What is inferred inside the framework
Failure modes / uncertainty / next validation needed

forbidden_transformations.bad: The framework proves discreteness emerges from ratchet events.
forbidden_transformations.good: Within the framework, ratchet events are defined as the mechanism by which continuous deformation pressure is converted into discrete stabilization outcomes.
This provides a framework-internal analogy to Planck-scale breakdown, where admissibility failure is interpreted as rebound rather than terminal collapse.
The framework models topology and geometry as recursively co-conditioning under ⇔_x.
Within the tested simulation regime, the result did not falsify the declared internal expectation.

fail_if: Any universal claim appears without evidence class.
Any analogy is written as identity.
Any simulation result is presented as external proof.
Any framework definition is presented as physical fact.
Any failure mode is omitted from a report.
Any term such as proves/solves/confirms appears without certification.
pass_if: Every external comparison is marked as comparison.
Every simulation result includes tested regime.
Every interpretation is separated from observation.
Every failure or uncertainty remains visible.
